newsitem.title: ITALY: "Structural" Italy budget to hit waste -Treasury.
newsitem.headline: "Structural" Italy budget to hit waste -Treasury.

text.p: Italy's 1997 budget, approved by the cabinet last week, includes numerous structural measures which will reduce inefficiency and waste in the public sector, the undersecretary at the Treasury said on Tuesday.
The budget package will slice an estimated 62.5 trillion lire off next year's projected deficit and contains 25 trillion lire of planned savings in state spending.
"These measures aren't just one-offs, but strucutural changes that will bring much larger savings in the years ahead," undersecretary Laura Pennacchi told a news conference.
Among examples cited was a reorganisation of hospitals and health care that was expected to raise 560 trillion lire next year, one trillion lire in 1998 and 1.4 trillion in 1999.
Pennacchi said the package, which still has to be approved by parliament, would also aim to reduce inefficiency in the public sector.
"Savings derived from cutting out waste, reducing inefficiency, rationalisations etc...will raise between three and five trillion lire," Pennacchi said.
She added that some of the government policies, such as converting some full time jobs into part-time positions, were "revolutionary".

And she stressed that the budget, twice the size of the originally planned package, would reduce Italy's deficit to gross domestic prodict (GDP) ratio to three percent next year, as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty.
"Italy will have all its papers in order to enter (the single European currency) from the first," she said. -- Crispian Balmer +396 6782501
